# Tenpai

<!-- AI-GENERATED by Claude (Claude Code), 2026-09-17 -->
<!-- Why: Project tooling and setup so study time goes to Flutter code. -->

Learn Japanese Riichi Mahjong from zero, Duolingo-style: short lessons, a
progression path, immediate feedback. Android only.

A school project: the real deliverable is the author learning Flutter. Claude
(Claude Code) is tutor and reviewer, not the author of `lib/`; everything it
wrote is listed in [docs/AI_CONTRIBUTIONS.md](docs/AI_CONTRIBUTIONS.md).

## Features

- **Lesson path** — seven units, from reading the tiles to scoring a hand:
  Déchiffrer les tuiles, Familles et suites, Les briques d'une main, La table,
  Le déroulé d'une partie, Gagner, Le score.
- **Four block types** — explanation, quiz, drill (« touch every tile that… »)
  and interactive (« complete the group »).
- **Retry until right** — a miss shows « Réessayer » and never reveals the
  answer; a lesson ends only when every block is right.
- **Sensei** — an AI explanation after a quiz or drill miss, in a panel that
  never blocks the lesson. It explains the mistake without naming the answer.
- **Yaku Dex** — the catalog of scoring hands, fetched from a REST API.
- **Tile scanner** — photograph a tile, get its card.
- **Account and progress** — email or Google sign-in, a two-question
  onboarding, XP and progress synced across devices.
- **Light and dark mode**.

## Tech stack

| Area | Package | Used for |

| UI | Flutter 3.47, `material_ui` | Material widgets (now outside the framework) |
| | `flutter_svg` | tile art |

| Navigation | `go_router` | routes and the tab shell |
| Models | `freezed`, `json_serializable` | immutable models, sealed unions, JSON |
| Network | `dio` | the yaku REST catalog |

| Local database | `isar_community` | settings, scan history, yaku cache |
| Backend | `firebase_auth` | email and Google sign-in |
| | `cloud_firestore` | progress and profile, synced offline-first |
| | `firebase_app_check` | only the genuine app reaches Firebase |
| | `firebase_ai` | the Sensei and tile recognition (Gemini, no API key in the app) |

## Assignment requirements

| Requirement | What Tenpai does | Code | Try it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Public REST API** | Loads the yaku catalog, a JSON API hosted on GitHub Pages | `lib/yaku/yaku_remote_source.dart` | Yaku Dex tab |
| **BaaS** | Firebase: accounts, database, Security Rules, App Check | `lib/auth/`<br>`firestore.rules` | Sign in or sign up |
| **Camera** | Photographs one tile and identifies it | `lib/scanner/tile_photo_source_impl.dart`<br>`lib/scanner/firebase_tile_identifier.dart` | Scanner tab |
| **AI feature** | The Sensei explains a mistake without giving the answer | `lib/sensei/` | Miss a quiz or drill → « Pourquoi ? » |
| **Local database** | Isar keeps settings, scan history and the yaku cache on the device | `lib/local/`<br>`lib/*/isar_*.dart` | Profil → history; Yaku Dex offline |
| **Cloud sync** | Firestore stores progress and syncs it, offline included | `lib/progress/firestore_progress_repository.dart` | Finish a lesson, sign in on another device |

Progress lives in Firestore, device-only data in Isar; they never hold the
same data.

**Why the REST API is self-hosted.** No public API serves Riichi Mahjong
yaku, and a weather or place API has nothing to do with learning the game.
So the catalog is published as a public, read-only JSON API from its own
repository, [Code-Nam/tenpai-api](https://github.com/Code-Nam/tenpai-api),
on GitHub Pages: anyone can call
`GET https://code-nam.github.io/tenpai-api/yaku/v1/catalog.json` without a
key. The app treats it like any third-party API: `dio` over HTTPS, a
versioned path (`v1`), a base URL injected at build time, timeouts, and an
Isar cache so the Yaku Dex still works offline.

## Project structure

The code is cut **by feature**, not by layer: each feature folder holds
everything that feature needs, and the file suffix gives each file's role.
Three folders are not features: `app/` wires the app together, `local/`
opens the database, and `shared/` holds what several features use.

```text
lib/
  main.dart                       startup: Firebase, App Check, Isar
  app/                            app shell: MaterialApp, routes, config
  auth/  onboarding/  learning/
  progress/  profile/  sensei/
  scanner/  yaku/  settings/      one folder per feature
  local/                          the Isar database instance
  shared/                         models, theme, widgets used by several features
assets/                           lessons (JSON), tiles (SVG), fonts
test/                             mirrors lib/, plus fakes/ and content/
firebase/rules-test/              tests for the Firestore rules
design/                           the designer handoff, source of truth for the UI
docs/                             milestone plans, roadmap, AI register
tool/check_conventions.dart       checks what lints cannot: file and class names,
                                  privacy, AI markers
.claude/                          Claude Code setup: review agents, the lib/ write guard
firestore.rules                   Firestore Security Rules
CLAUDE.md                         the working rules given to Claude
```

Inside a feature folder, the suffix says what a file is:

| Suffix | Role |
|---|---|
| `_screen.dart` | a screen |
| `_widget.dart` | a reusable widget (in `widgets/` when there are several) |
| `_providers.dart` | the feature's Riverpod providers |
| `_repository.dart` | the interface screens depend on; its implementation is `_repository_impl.dart` or named after its backend (`firebase_auth_repository.dart`, `isar_settings_repository.dart`) |
| `_source.dart` | where data comes from: REST, Isar, bundled assets |
| `_record.dart` | an Isar collection |
| no suffix | the feature's models and states (`yaku.dart`, `lesson_session.dart`, `scan_state.dart`) |

Tests replace repositories and sources with the hand-written fakes in
`test/fakes/`. `lib/firebase_options.dart` is git-ignored and provided with
the submission.

## How to start the project

You need Flutter 3.47+ and an Android emulator or device. No emulator yet?
See the guide for [macOS](docs/macos-emulator.md),
[Linux](docs/linux-emulator.md) or [WSL2 on Windows](docs/wsl-emulator.md).

1. Copy the three files provided with the submission:
   - `google-services.json` → `android/app/`
   - `firebase_options.dart` → `lib/`
   - `dart_defines.json` → the repository root (next to `pubspec.yaml`)
2. Install and generate:

   ```bash
   flutter pub get
   dart run build_runner build -d
   ```

3. Run:

   ```bash
   flutter run --dart-define-from-file=dart_defines.json
   ```

   In VS Code, the launch configurations already pass that file.

## Setup

Only needed to run Tenpai on **your own** Firebase project.

1. **Firebase console**
   - Authentication: enable Email/Password and Google, and register the
     debug SHA-1 (`keytool -list -v -keystore ~/.android/debug.keystore
     -alias androiddebugkey -storepass android`).
   - Firestore: production mode, region `europe-west1`.
   - App Check: Play Integrity, plus one debug token (*Manage debug tokens*
     → *Add debug token*) shared by every debug build.
2. **Firebase files** — run `flutterfire configure --platforms=android`, or
   download `google-services.json` from the console. The app starts Firebase
   from `lib/firebase_options.dart`, so the « google-services was not
   applied » warning at startup is expected.
   <details><summary>If <code>flutterfire configure</code> cannot see your project</summary>

   Write `lib/firebase_options.dart` by hand from `google-services.json`:
   `apiKey` = `client[0].api_key[0].current_key`, `appId` =
   `client[0].client_info.mobilesdk_app_id`, `messagingSenderId` =
   `project_info.project_number`, `projectId` = `project_info.project_id`,
   `storageBucket` = `project_info.storage_bucket`.
   </details>
3. **Firestore rules**

   ```bash
   firebase deploy --only firestore:rules
   # test them locally (Java + `npm install` in firebase/rules-test):
   firebase emulators:exec --only firestore "npm --prefix firebase/rules-test test"
   ```

4. **`dart_defines.json`** — git-ignored, at the repository root:

   ```json
   {
     "YAKU_BASE_URL": "https://code-nam.github.io/tenpai-api/",
     "APP_CHECK_DEBUG_TOKEN": "<the debug token from step 1>"
   }
   ```

   The yaku catalog is served by GitHub Pages from
   [Code-Nam/tenpai-api](https://github.com/Code-Nam/tenpai-api); keep the
   trailing slash. The app refuses to start without it. Without the token,
   each new emulator prints its own in logcat and must be allowed by hand.
   Revoke the token once it is no longer needed: anyone holding it passes
   App Check with a debug build.
